newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares rise on New York, Autoliv surges.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares rise on New York, Autoliv surges.

text.p: Swedish shares ended higher on Tuesday as a stronger U.S. market helped them recover from Monday's fall.
The general index rose 1.67 percent to 3,183.18 in turnover of 5.07 billion crowns.
"We will probably have to get used to trade being a bit jerky," a dealer said. "Volatility will probably remain high but the underlying trend is upwards."
Car safety equipment Autoliv was a winner, up 20 crowns to 307.5 after Goldman Sachs put it on its recommended list with a target price of $43 a share in three to six months.
"Many are positive to the share and when Autoliv starts picking up nobody wants to let go of it," a dealer said.
Truck maker Kalmar Industries rocketed 17 crowns to 165 after news of merging with Finnish cargo handling and building materials group Partek's subsidiary STS.
"All in all it looks positive," a dealer said. "They are creating a larger player on a market that needs restructuring."
Banking group Handelsbanken, insurer Trygg-Hansa and rubber and mining group Trelleborg took different directions after releasing six months earnings.

Handelsbanken rose 4.5 to 252 on a higher than expected profit, Trygg-Hansa dropped four crowns to 170, partly because of some fears of overdependency on equity moves, and Trelleborg edged 0.5 crown higher to 128.
Insurer Skandia surged 17 crowns to 332 ahead of releasing six-month figures on Wednesday.
Heavyweights telecoms group Ericsson and drugs group Astra were also pulled up in the general rebound with Ericsson jumping 8.5 crowns to 356 and Astra rising one crown to 133.5.
